# NetCoop AI — Evaluation Results

**Dataset:** 13 scenarios, entirely **synthetic** (generated by `scripts/gen_scenarios.py` with a fixed random seed; no production campus network data was used or is required). Ground truth is documented in `scenarios/ground_truth.json` and read only by this script, never by the diagnosis pipeline itself.

`rules.yaml` was **not** tuned against these results in this evaluation step.

## Metrics

| Metric | NetCoop pipeline | Naive baseline |
|---|---|---|
| Root-cause accuracy | 100% | 100% |
| Affected-device accuracy | 100% | 100% |
| Correct abstention rate | 100% | 0% |
| False confident diagnoses | 0/4 (0%) | 4/4 (100%) |
| Average checks used | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| Mean latency (s) | 0.0135 | 0.0003 |
| Overall status accuracy | 100% | 69% |

Root-cause and affected-device accuracy are computed over the 9 scenario(s) ground truth expects to be diagnosed. Correct abstention rate and false confident diagnoses are computed over the 4 scenario(s) ground truth expects to need abstention (`insufficient_evidence` or `invalid_input`).

## Per-scenario results

| scenario | expected | pipeline status | pipeline cause | baseline status | baseline cause |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| normal | diagnosed | diagnosed ✓ | No fault detected | diagnosed ✓ | No fault detected |
| congestion | diagnosed | diagnosed ✓ | Link congestion | diagnosed ✓ | Link congestion |
| interface_fault | diagnosed | diagnosed ✓ | Interface or cabling fault on a single link | diagnosed ✓ | Interface or cabling fault on a single link |
| weak_wifi | diagnosed | diagnosed ✓ | Weak wireless signal | diagnosed ✓ | Weak wireless signal |
| dns_dhcp_failure | diagnosed | diagnosed ✓ | DNS or DHCP service failure | diagnosed ✓ | DNS or DHCP service failure |
| cpu_overload | diagnosed | diagnosed ✓ | Device CPU overload | diagnosed ✓ | Device CPU overload |
| hardware_failure | diagnosed | diagnosed ✓ | Hardware failure | diagnosed ✓ | Hardware failure |
| upstream_failure | diagnosed | diagnosed ✓ | Link congestion | diagnosed ✓ | Link congestion |
| simultaneous | diagnosed | diagnosed ✓ | Weak wireless signal | diagnosed ✓ | Interface or cabling fault on a single link |
| insufficient | insufficient_evidence | insufficient_evidence ✓ | — | diagnosed ✗ | No fault detected |
| stale | insufficient_evidence | insufficient_evidence ✓ | — | diagnosed ✗ | Interface or cabling fault on a single link |
| contradictory | insufficient_evidence | insufficient_evidence ✓ | — | diagnosed ✗ | No fault detected |
| ambiguous_loss | insufficient_evidence | insufficient_evidence ✓ | — | diagnosed ✗ | Interface or cabling fault on a single link |

## Notes

- The naive baseline is a single-pass threshold classifier reading raw metric values directly off the latest record in each file -- no `EvidenceStore`/grounding, no topology, no targeted checks, and **no abstention** (it always commits to a specific cause). Its false-confident-diagnoses rate is the clearest illustration of why `insufficient_evidence` exists as a status.
- This run deliberately doesn't supply a `--checks` directory, so "average checks used" is 0 for both systems: `ground_truth.json`'s `expected_status` documents the no-checks baseline (several test suites already assert against it that way), and enabling checks here would silently resolve `stale`/`insufficient`/`ambiguous_loss` to `diagnosed`, disagreeing with that ground truth for no good reason. Targeted checks resolving exactly those three scenarios are proven separately in `tests/test_milestone6.py` and via `python -m netcoop run ... --checks scenarios/checks/<name>`.
- Affected-device accuracy counts a prediction correct if it overlaps ground truth's device set at all, since the pipeline documented-ly reports its single strongest device for multi-device incidents rather than every affected device.
